# rtists <a href="https://astamm.github.io/rtists/"><img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" alt="rtists website" /></a>

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/astamm/rtists/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/astamm/rtists/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/astamm/rtists/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/astamm/rtists)
[![pkgdown](https://github.com/astamm/rtists/workflows/pkgdown/badge.svg)](https://github.com/astamm/rtists/actions)
<!-- badges: end -->

**rtists** (*R for Tissue Integrity Superimposed on Tractography Streamlines*)
provides interactive 3-D visualisation of tractography streamlines and bundles
defined in the [riot](https://github.com/astamm/riot) package.

The main function is `plot3d()`, an [S7](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/)
generic with methods for both `riot::streamline` and `riot::bundle` objects.
Figures are rendered by [plotly](https://plotly.com/r/) and are fully
interactive (pan, rotate, zoom).

## Installation

Install the development version from [GitHub](https://github.com/astamm/rtists):

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("astamm/rtists")
```

## Usage

### Build some riot objects

```{r}
#| label: create-objects
library(rtists)
library(riot)

pts <- matrix(
  c(
    0, 0, 0,
    1, 2, 1,
    2, 3, 3,
    3, 3, 5,
    4, 2, 6,
    5, 1, 7
  ),
  ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(NULL, c("X", "Y", "Z"))
)

sl <- new_streamline(
  points          = pts,
  point_data      = list(FA = c(0.25, 0.40, 0.65, 0.70, 0.55, 0.30)),
  streamline_data = list(mean_FA = 0.475)
)

set.seed(42)
bun <- new_bundle(lapply(seq_len(6), function(i) {
  noise <- matrix(rnorm(nrow(pts) * 3, sd = 0.2), ncol = 3)
  colnames(noise) <- c("X", "Y", "Z")
  new_streamline(
    points          = pts + noise,
    point_data      = list(FA = pmin(pmax(sl@point_data$FA + rnorm(6, sd = 0.05), 0), 1)),
    streamline_data = list(mean_FA = mean(sl@point_data$FA))
  )
}))
```

### `plot3d()` — colour modes

#### Default: orientation colours

Each point is coloured by the direction of the local tangent vector using the
standard DTI convention (left–right = red, anterior–posterior = green,
superior–inferior = blue):

```{r}
#| label: orientation
plot3d(bun)
```

#### Colour by per-point metadata

Pass any key from `@point_data` to map a continuous scalar to a colour scale:

```{r}
#| label: point-fa
plot3d(bun, color = "FA", palette = "Viridis")
```

#### Colour by per-streamline metadata

Keys from `@streamline_data` are broadcast to all points of each streamline,
giving every tract a single uniform colour:

```{r}
#| label: streamline-fa
plot3d(bun, color = "mean_FA", palette = "RdYlBu")
```

#### Fixed colour

Any CSS colour name or hex code colours all lines identically:

```{r}
#| label: fixed
plot3d(bun, color = "steelblue", opacity = 0.7, linewidth = 3)
```

## Colour modes at a glance

| `color` value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `"orientation"` (default) | Per-point RGB from local fibre direction |
| Name of a `@point_data` key | Continuous or categorical scale per point |
| Name of a `@streamline_data` key | Uniform colour per streamline |
| CSS / hex string (e.g. `"steelblue"`) | Fixed colour for all lines |

Additional arguments (`palette`, `linewidth`, `opacity`, `...`) are documented
in `?plot3d`.
